 O R D E R:

Justice Surjit Singh, President (Oral) By this common order, we proceed to dispose of two appeals, particulars whereof are given in the heading of this order, as both the appeals arise out of the same order, i.e. order dated 28th May, 2009, of learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Kangra at Dharamshala. Appeal No.208/2009, has been filed by Bishan Dass, who was the complainant before the learned District Forum, in a complaint under section 12 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, while appeal No.243/2009, has been filed by M/S Sarvpriya Autos Bye Pass Dalhousie Road, Pathankot, who was one of the opposite parties, in the aforesaid complaint.

2. Facts relevant for the disposal of the appeals may be noticed. Complainant Bishan Dass, purchased a Swaraj Mazda Samrat truck, for a sum of `7.15 lacs, from M/S Sarvpriya Autos Bye Pass Dalhousie Road, Pathankot, impleaded as opposite party No.1 in the complaint, on 27.04.2006. Manufacturer of the said vehicle is Swaraj Mazda Limited, impleaded as opposite party No.2, in the complaint. According to the complainant, the truck had a manufacturing defect. It started giving problem, within a few days of its purchase. It would not move smoothly on hilly roads, as it had picking problem. Defect was brought to the notice of opposite party No.1, i.e. M/S Sarvpriya Autos, from whom it had been purchased. The said opposite party did not remove the defect nor did it replace the vehicle. Complainant then filed a complaint, under section 12 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, seeking issuance of a direction to the opposite parties to remove the defect or to replace the vehicle with a new one and also to pay `1.00 lac, by way of compensation, on account of financial loss sustained by him because of the truck having remained stationary.

3. Separate replies were filed by both the opposite parties. It was denied that the truck had any manufacturing defect. It was stated that the truck was misused by the appellant, inasmuch as, he had been overloading the vehicle, even in hilly terrains and because of that, it developed the problem of picking, whenever there was an ascent. It was also stated that the complainant was not a consumer, inasmuch as, the vehicle had been purchased for commercial purpose. Jurisdiction of the District Forum was also challenged on the ground that neither the opposite parties resided or had their place of business within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Forum, nor had any part of cause of action taken place, within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Forum.

4. Learned District Forum concluded that the District Forum had the jurisdiction. With regard to the plea that the complainant was not a consumer, as the vehicle was purchased for commercial purpose, learned District Forum held that if the goods developed a defect during warranty period and the defect is not removed or repair is not carried out within the warranty period, then the buyer of the goods will be a consumer, even if the goods are purchased for commercial purpose. In support of this view reliance has been placed by the learned District Forum on a judgment of the Honble National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, New Delhi, but without giving the complete citation. Only the name of the case is mentioned in the order and the same is View Tech Imaging Equipment Pvt. Ltd. And another versus CMC Ltd., and another. Learned District Forum further held that this was a case of deficiency in service, as the defect pointed out within the warranty period, had not been removed and passed the order directing both the opposite patties to remove the defect in the vehicle and also to pay `25,000/-, as compensation and `5,000/- as litigation cost.

5. Complainant is aggrieved by the relief granted by the learned District Forum. He prays for the grant of relief of replacement of vehicle by a new one or the refund of the price of the vehicle, besides claiming damages to the tune of `1.00 lac. Second appeal has been filed by one of the opposite parties, i.e. the dealer from whom the vehicle was purchased. Said appellant is aggrieved by the findings that the District Forum had the territorial jurisdiction, complainant was a consumer and the truck was defective, as also the final order directing it to repair the vehicle and to pay damages and litigation cost.

6. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the record.

7. Complainant himself stated in the complaint that he had purchased the vehicle for business purpose. No doubt, in the affidavit, which he filed by way of evidence, he did state that he had purchased the vehicle for earning his livelihood, but that cannot be taken into account for the simple reason that evidence adduced without making an averment in the pleadings, does not carry much weightage. In any case, even in the said affidavit, complainant did not say that he had purchased the vehicle to earn his livelihood by self employing himself. So, he does not qualify as a consumer.

8. Next submission made on behalf of the complainant is that when goods are purchased even for commercial purpose and the seller gives warranty, the purchaser will be a consumer if the seller does not repair the goods within the warranty period. This submission also merits rejection for two reasons. First the relief claimed by complainant is based on the allegation that the vehicle is defective and it requires replacement. He has not pleaded that there has been any deficiency in service. In any case, in the present appeal, he seeks reversal of the order of the learned District Forum for the repair of the vehicle and prays for the replacement of the vehicle or the refund of the price of the vehicle, which leaves no doubt that his grievance, is that the vehicle is defective and it requires replacement.

9. Even if, it be assumed that his grievance is about deficiency in service, because of non-repairing of the vehicle within warranty period, in that situation also, he will not be a consumer. By an amendment carried out in section 2(1) (d) (ii) of Consumer Protection Act, 1986, effective from June, 2003, legislature has excluded from the purview of consumer even the hirer of service, if such service is hired for commercial purpose.

Taking this view in another case, i.e. M/S Allengers Medical Systems Limited versus Beena Sharma, First Appeal No.40/2010, decided on 07.05.2012, we have held that if the goods are purchased for commercial purpose with warranty and the repair is not carried out within the warranty period to the satisfaction of the buyer, the buyer would not be a consumer if the goods were purchased for commercial purpose, because of the aforesaid amendment carried out in the definition of consumer in the year 2003. In that case, we have distinguished two judgments of the Honble National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in case Pearlite Liners Ltd., versus Thermo Jarrell Ash Corporation and another 2006 CTJ 891 (CP) (NCDRC) & East India Construction Co. versus Modern Consultancy Services and others 2006 CTJ 996 (CP) (NCDRC), in which it had been held that if the repair is not carried out within the warranty period, that will be a case of deficiency in service and the buyer of the goods would be a consumer, even if the goods were purchased for commercial purpose. We have distinguished the aforesaid judgments, as the goods in those cases were purchased prior to the amendment of 2003, in the definition of consumer.

10. As a result of the above discussion, we hold that the complainant is not a consumer.

11. As regards the opposite partys objection to the jurisdiction of the District Forum, admittedly, the opposite parties do not reside or have their places of business within the jurisdiction of the learned District Forum. Vehicle was also purchased outside the jurisdiction of the learned District Forum. Opposite parties have their places of business and their residences in the state of Punjab. No doubt, the vehicle developed a snag within the jurisdiction of learned District Forum or it was registered with the Registering & Licencing Authority Kangra that in our considered view cannot be treated as a part of the cause of action, vesting the learned District Forum Kangra with jurisdiction to decide the dispute.

12. Consequently, we are of the considered view that the learned District Forum did not have the territorial jurisdiction to entertain the complaint.

13. As a result of the above discussion, we accept the appeal filed by M/S Sarvpriya Autos, opposite party No.1, set aside the impugned order of the leaned District Forum and dismiss the complaint. As a sequel to the allowing of appeal filed by M/S Sarvpriya Autos, the second appeal, which has been filed by the complainant, becomes infructuous. So, the same is dismissed.

14. This order shall be placed on the record of F.A. No. 208/2009 and its one authenticated copy, on the record of F.A. No.243/2009.

15. One copy of this order be sent to each of the parties, free of cost, as per Rules.
